rights_basis: Quotes the 1870 French of Chabas' complete translation of Papyrus Sallier IV (public domain), from a hash-pinned OCR of the Bayerische Staatsbibliothek digitisation, with an independent English rendering. No modern copyrighted edition (Bakir 1966 and successors) is reproduced.
scope_note: Thirty-two day entries whose day assignment was verified line-by-line against hOCR bounding boxes, of which eighteen carry an explicit birth prognosis. This is a hemerology of the 365-day civil year, not a horoscopy: the prognosis attaches to the civil day of birth alone and involves no celestial position. Accents are omitted from the French quotations because the retrieved OCR layer does not carry them reliably; the quotations are otherwise verbatim.

known_limits.day_marks_not_encoded: Chabas reproduces each day's three-part mark in hieroglyphs. The OCR layer cannot resolve them, so no per-day mark value is asserted here; only the mark system, which Chabas states in French prose, is encoded as rules.
known_limits.orthography: OCR-sourced French is unaccented and may carry residual character errors; the printed page and scan number are given for every entry so any claim can be checked against the facsimile.
known_limits.lacunae: Ellipses reproduce Chabas' own lacuna marks.

entries.french_chabas_1870: Ne mets pas d'encens sur le feu en ce jour; ne tue pas de betail, pas de chevres, pas de canards; ne mange pas d'oie; cela a vecu. N'ecoute pas de chants joyeux en ce jour; le coeur de l'ennemi de Ra s'est affermi... sur les choses qu'il a faites pour ses enfants. Quiconque est ne ce jour-la, ne vit pas.
entries.engine_rendering: Put no incense on the fire on this day; kill no cattle, no goats, no ducks; eat no goose - that has lived. Listen to no joyful songs on this day; the heart of Ra's enemy has grown strong ... over the things he did to his children. Whoever is born on that day does not live.
entries.day_assignment_evidence: Two-column hOCR bounding boxes were read directly: the day cell's baseline sits within 30px of the first line of this legend, and no intervening day cell exists. Where the cell preserved its Gregorian equivalent the Egyptian date was independently recomputed from Chabas' Coptic anchor and agreed.

entries.french_chabas_1870: La majeste de Ra vogue a l'aide du vent, du coucher au lever. Ce fut dans cette circonstance qu'il monta dans son arche divine. Quiconque est ne ce jour-la meurt venere par les citoyens de Ptah-Ka-Ha (Memphis) de Sekhet, Naken, Nefer et Tum; ils seront heureux devant le dieu qui y reside, Ptah. Offrandes a son nom en ce jour.
entries.engine_rendering: The majesty of Ra sails with the help of the wind, from setting to rising. It was on that occasion that he went up into his divine bark. Whoever is born on that day dies revered by the citizens of Ptah-Ka-Ha (Memphis), of Sekhet, Naken, Nefer and Tum; they will be happy before the god who dwells there, Ptah. Offerings in his name on this day.

Ces dieux furent avec Thoth a frapper l'ennemi Set par devant et par derriere, dans sa forteresse; la, il se fit un carnage furieux ce jour-la. Quiconque est ne ce jour-la, meurt (ayant a la main) du pain et de la liqueur haq a la bouche, et l'oeil dessus.

Whoever is born on that day dies (with in his hand) bread and haq-liquor at his mouth, and his eye upon it.
